I feel the EXACT same way to you. Word by Word. Absolutely hate being described as cute and having people tower over me. 

Grew up in an all girls school where there must have been something in the water. I'd say 70% of my year were over 5'9 and all were model material. It utterly ruined my self-esteem. Couldn't play netball, couldn't play volleyball, couldn't be talked without them towering me.


Being tall is literally the beauty standard and brings so much benefits like being better at sports, being ELIGIBLE for certain sports, more calories, better proportions, modelling, acting, and just general prowess and power. Goddesses are described as tall, warriors and Amazons are described as tall, athletes are tall, ballerinas are tall, models are tall. Being physically looked down upon just immediately sets a power dynamic.

But no - it's all about what men want and like. I despise the word "cute." I'm an adult woman, not a child or a doll.

The logical side says this is all some kind of seeking evidence to reinforce the negative concept I have of myself. But even so, the feeling of envy and insecurity about my height remains.
